correctness.rationale: The complete 11-vertex graph and ordinary cut facets are explicit. Exact exhaustive face enumeration gives 123 disconnected triples and dual f-vector (11,55,42,9). Three signed integer boundary matrices reduce by unimodular unit pivots to ranks 10,32,9 with entirely zero remaining blocks, yielding torsion-free dual first-homology rank 13 and second-homology rank one, hence via integral Alexander duality a degree-six integral class of rank one and degree-seven rank 13 and no other reduced groups. Explicit 18-triangle integer cycle has zero boundary and nontrivial mod3 dual H2 class. All 12 graph automorphisms are generated from degree-neighbor signatures, the rank-one sign action is tested mod3, and signed dual Lefschetz yields the entire character; independently enumerated original-complex Lefschetz traces agree for all 12 elements. Pure 7-dimensional complex has nonzero degree-six homology, so not shellable.

value.rationale: The Herschel graph is the canonical smallest non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph. Its nine intersecting squares give a natural sharp geometric situation not covered by the strongest existing disjoint-square three-cut homotopy theorem. The full torsion-free two-degree homology and D6 character distinguish this complex from the usual top-degree sphere-wedge behavior, certify non-shellability, and show both global fixed subspaces vanish—information absent from simple Betti tables. The theorem has a definite mathematical object, full invariant and reproducible proof, without unsupported claims of wider generality.
